data.summary: added: Preprint: Capturing additional variance in impact of adolescent depression from free text: proof of concept and preliminary results

after.title: Preprint: Capturing additional variance in impact of adolescent depression from free text: proof of concept and preliminary results
after.authors: Matar, A. Y.; Lossio-Ventura, J. A.; Pereira, F.; Nielson, D. M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Machine Learning Core, National Institute of Mental Health, NIH
after.abstract: Depression in adolescents has grown in prevalence in the past decade. Despite indications of differences in symptom presentation, measurement properties, and treatment response between adolescents and adults, research is dominated by adult participants. Qualitative work has identified symptomatic and functional domains important to depressed adolescents and those around them; however, there remains little quantitative evidence of how these domains relate to the functional impact of the disorder. In this preregistered study, we use adolescent self-report (n = 153) and parent-report (n = 106) responses in the depression section of the Development and Well-Being Assessment (DAWBA) to examine what information relevant to reported depression impact may be missing from its structured symptom-scale. We apply Large Language Models (LLMs) to participant free-text answers to extract information on a taxonomy of 80 outcomes. Through a sequential residual stacking framework that estimates incremental information in symptom sum-scores (S ), item-level symptom-scale answers (Q), and LLM-derived text representations (T ), we find that parent text contains information relevant to their report of depression impact that is not available in the structured symptom-scale, with the largest contributions concentrated in functioning-related domains (e.g., professional responsibilities, social exclusion, autonomy, coping). No such evidence was found in adolescent self-reports. Given the moderate sample size, these results are preliminary. Nonetheless, we provide a proof-of-concept framework for extracting information from open-ended free text in large existing datasets, and estimating incremental information across sources, which could be applied to uncover specific aspects of adolescent mental disorders across populations.

after.authors: Alves, H.; Carvalheiro, R.; Jardim Santos, C.; Silva, J. P.; Hirsch, J. A.; Michael, Y.; Moreira, C.; Ribeiro, A. I.
after.abstract: Objective: Urban neighbourhoods across Europe are rapidly transforming through gentrification, with Portuguese cities particularly affected. Although the health impacts of these changes are increasingly recognised, validated instruments to assess perceptions of neighbourhood change remain scarce. This study adapted and validated a Portuguese version of the Perceptions About Change in Environment and Residents (PACER-PT) scale. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 255 adults living for >=5yrs in the Lisbon and Porto Metropolitan Areas. PACER was translated and culturally adapted to create PACER-PT. We evaluated psychometric properties using exploratory factor analysis (EFA), internal consistency, and convergent and criterion validity. Results: EFA identified a three-factor structure explaining 47.5% of the variance: Built, social and economic changes, Positive attitude towards neighbourhood changes, and Displacement concerns and neighbourhood disruption. Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach s alpha=0.70-0.78). Convergent/criterion validity were supported by significant associations with amount and pace of change, self-rated health, and quality of life. Younger and wealthier participants and those with greater residential satisfaction reported more favourable perceptions. Conclusions: PACER-PT demonstrated it is a valid instrument for assessing gentrification-related neighbourhood changes in Portugal.

after.authors: Alsaied, M. A.; Hegazy, M.; Saleh, M. M.; Barakat, B.; Ibrahim, O. R.; Abdelrazek, H. M.; Nazemi, S.; El-Hussuna, A.; Shalaby, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Associate Professor of Surgery, Colorectal Surgery Unit, Department of General Surgery, Mansoura University Hospitals, Mansoura University, Mansoura, Egypt
after.abstract: Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA). Databases were screened for DTA studies of MRI-based radiomics predicting TDs in adult RC patients with histopathology as reference. Results: Nine studies (2589 patients) were identified. Across included studies, the bivariate meta-analysis showed pooled sensitivity of 0.765 (95% CI 0.714 - 0.809) and specificity of 0.790 (95% CI 0.750 - 0.825), with overall AUC of 0.845 and very low heterogeneity (I2 = 7.3%). In validation datasets, diagnostic performance remained consistent (AUC 0.806), with pooled sensitivity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809) and specificity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809). For MRI modality, T2 weighted image (T2WI) showed higher sensitivity (0.745) than T2WI plus diffusion weighted image (DWI) (0.697), while T2WI+DWI had higher specificity (0.809 vs 0.737) and AUC (0.829 vs 0.796), with no significant subgroup differences (p[≥]0.192). Models combining radiomics with clinical/radiological variables achieved significantly higher sensitivity (0.842 vs 0.657, p<0.001) and higher AUC (0.827 vs 0.752), with comparable specificity. Conclusion: MRI-based radiomics demonstrates good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in RC. The integration of radiomics with clinical or imaging features increases the accuracy of identification. Amongst the MRI modalities, models that utilize the combination of T2WI plus DWI are more accurate than those using T2WI or DWI only.

after.authors: Du, X.; Lyu, Z.; Libre, M. A.; Reynolds, M. J.; Rodriguez, D. M.; Liu, Z. E.; Lian, B. Q.; Zhou, L.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Brigham and Women's Hospital/Harvard Medical School
after.abstract: Background: Dementia is frequently underdiagnosed in primary care, with fewer than half of cases identified and only 8-20% detected at early stages. Our objective is to develop an Agentic AI-powered clinical decision support systems (CDSS) maintaining the patient's virtual cognitive status and provide physicians with ready-to-use summaries and next step suggestions. Methods: We developed MERIT (Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care) via participatory co-design with primary care provider. It maintains a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's electronic health records (EHR) and conversation with the patient and provide clinical decision support based on it. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) was employed by the system to retrieve dementia-related risk factors from multimodal EHR. Additionally, we used reflection Agentic AI design pattern to improve quality of AI Agent generated text. We used one PCP's patient data to optimize the system, then used patients from another four PCPs for testing. We mainly used expert manual evaluation based on 5-point Likert-Scales. For readability of patient summary and personalized education material, besides manual evaluation, we also employed widely used Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch We-Kincaid Grade Level. Results: MERIT has four modulars: 1) patient conversation agent; 2) patient virtual cognitive status maintainer; 3) personalized education provider; and 4) decision support provider. Our evaluation focused on the provider-facing part, which relies on EHR without involving any patient conversation. The evaluation on the testing data demonstrates good performance. On a 5-point Likert scale, in the test set, patient virtual cognitive status summaries received average scores of 4.0 (SD 0.74) for correctness, 4.2 (SD 0.59) for completeness, 4.3 (SD 0.59) for readability, and 4.1 (SD 0.71) for clinical usefulness; clinical decision support received 3.9 (SD 0.87) for correctness, 4.3 (SD 0.66) for completeness, and 4.3 (SD 0.64) for adoptability; and the personalized education material received average ratings of 4.3 (SD 0.62) for completeness, 4.5 (SD 0.60) for readability, 4.3 (SD 0.78) for usefulness, and 4.4 (SD 0.49) for empathy. Automated readability assessment showed that patient summaries had a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 18.3 (SD 4.9) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.7 (SD 0.7), consistent with college-level text, whereas personalized patient education had a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50.1 (SD 7.1) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.7 (SD 1.5), which is high-school student understandable text. Conclusion: Our developed system MERIT can maintain a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's multimodal EHR, provide the patient with clear and readable personalized education materials, and provide the PCP with ready-to-use cognitive summaries and decision support with high adoptability. By integrating our CDSS into Epic in the near future, our developed system will largely benefit older adults with cognitive decline and slow down the progression.

Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) was employed by the system to retrieve dementia-related risk factors from multimodal EHR. Additionally, we used reflection Agentic AI design pattern to improve quality of AI Agent generated text. We used one PCP's patient data to optimize the system, then used patients from another four PCPs for testing. We mainly used expert manual evaluation based on 5-point Likert-Scales. Automated readability assessment showed that patient summaries had a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 18.3 (SD 4.9) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.7 (SD 0.7), consistent with college-level text, whereas personalized patient education had a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50.1 (SD 7.1) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.7 (SD 1.5), which is high-school student understandable text. Conclusion: Our developed system MERIT can maintain a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's multimodal EHR, provide the patient with clear and readable personalized education materials, and provide the PCP with ready-to-use cognitive summaries and decision support with high adoptability. By integrating our CDSS into Epic in the near future, our developed system will largely benefit older adults with cognitive decline and slow down the progression.

after.abstract: Background & Objectives: As recently recommended by neuropathologists, we assessed the diagnostic accuracy of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) alpha-synuclein (-syn) seed amplification assay (SAA) in an autopsy cohort with systemic assessment of Lewy pathology. Methods: CSF was obtained antemortem and stored at -80 . -syn SAA and systemic Lewy pathology assessment were conducted as previously reported. Kinetic parameters, including maximum fluorescence (Fmax) and time to reach 50% of Fmax (T50), were also evaluated. Results: CSF samples were available from 30 patients (8 with symptomatic Lewy body disease [LBD], 2 with multiple system atrophy [MSA], 3 with Alzheimer's disease [AD], and 17 disease controls). Despite different clinical stages, all patients with LBD had diffuse neocortical or limbic-stage pathology at autopsy, with widespread peripheral Lewy bodies, including in the esophagus, heart, and sympathetic ganglia. Lewy pathology was not observed in disease controls. SAA was positive in all 8 with LBD, low positive in one patient with AD, and negative in all others. Fmax was significantly higher in LBD compared with cases without -syn pathology (9091{+/-}2083 vs. 1659{+/-}113 relative fluorescence units). The low-positive case had a lower positivity rate (25% vs. 75-100%), lower Fmax, and longer T50 than LBD cases. Conclusions: In this pilot study, CSF -syn SAA demonstrated high specificity (95%) and high sensitivity (100%) for detecting LBD; however, all LBD cases had widespread pathology, including peripheral involvement. Larger studies are needed to understand the association between CSF -syn SAA and Lewy pathology in the body.

after.abstract: Background Assessments of upper extremity control in ataxia are susceptible to measurement error and inherent variability. Objectives Quantify trial-to-trial variability in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) nose-to-finger (NTF) and finger chase (FC) tasks, and test agreement between scores derived from live assessment and retrospective video review. Methods 17 patients with cerebellar ataxia were video-recorded performing tasks behind a transparent, calibrated 1-cm grid. NTF tremor amplitude and FC undershoot/overshoot distance derived from live scores were compared with measurements from video review. Results NTF tremor amplitude and FC under/overshoot varied between consecutive trials. Patients received 2.4 {+/-} 0.7 (NTF) and 2.6 {+/-} 0.8 (FC) different SARA scores for limb excursions within one session. Live and video score match was NTF: 64.7% left, 70.6% right; FC: 64.7% left, 41.2% right. Live scoring often overestimated impairment. Conclusions Trial-to-trial variability and live/video discordance limit the precision of SARA upper-limb tasks.

after.abstract: Sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 influence dementia risk, but whether its molecular predictors differ across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata remains unclear. We investigated plasma proteomic and metabolomic signatures predicting future dementia in 43,759 UK Biobank participants across four sex-by-APOE {varepsilon}4 groups. The association between APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status and dementia differed by sex (interaction p = 0.027). Machine-learning models achieved higher discrimination in APOE {varepsilon}4 carriers (AUC 0.85-0.90) than non-carriers (AUC 0.74-0.76), with the highest performance in female carriers. Most top molecular predictors were subgroup-specific, including C7, CDON and EDIL3 in female carriers and KLK4, MMP12 and TGFBI in male carriers. When UK Biobank models were applied to the Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium, 12/17 available top predictors in female carriers and 10/16 in male carriers remained highly ranked. These findings identify distinct molecular signatures of dementia risk across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata, supporting stratified biomarker discovery.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Exercise and Nutrition Sciences Department, Milken Institute School of Public Health, The George Washington University, Washington, DC, USA
after.abstract: Background: Perimenopause is a transitional stage preceding menopause, characterized by hormonal fluctuations and physiological changes that may increase cardiometabolic risk. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiome may influence these changes through estrogen metabolism and microbial metabolite production. Inulin, a prebiotic fiber that modulates the gut microbiome, may offer a targeted nutritional strategy; however, its effects during perimenopause remain largely unexplored. Objective: This proof-of-concept study evaluates the effects of short-term inulin supplementation on gut microbiome composition, microbial metabolites, vascular function, skeletal muscle health, and metabolic flexibility in perimenopausal overweight women or with obesity. Methods: We will conduct a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled crossover trial among 27 women aged 40 to55 years. Participants will receive 10 g/day of inulin and a matched maltodextrin placebo for two 14-day intervention periods separated by a 2 to 4-week washout. We will assess changes in gut and vaginal microbiome composition and functional capacity, stool and plasma microbial metabolites, and circulating markers of estrogen metabolism as primary outcomes. We will also evaluate vascular function, skeletal muscle health and oxidative capacity, and metabolic flexibility as secondary outcomes. Additionally, we will assess physical activity, sleep, dietary intake, perimenopausal symptoms, and intervention feasibility, adherence, acceptability, and tolerability. Conclusion: This study will provide novel insights into the feasibility and biological effects of inulin supplementation on gut-host mechanisms and cardiometabolic health during perimenopause, informing the design of future larger-scale trials. Keywords: Gut Microbiome, Metabolome, Fiber, Women, Prebiotics, Clinical Trial Protocol, Inulin, Perimenopause, Healthy Aging

after.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of widespread, accessible viral surveillance to ensure pandemic-preparedness. The rapid diagnosis of respiratory infections is crucial not only for effective patient management but also to inform ongoing surveillance for the detection of outbreaks. Reverse transcriptase-Loop mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) assays are an attractive alternative to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for rapid, decentralised testing in resource limited settings due being rapid and low cost. Here we present the design and evaluation of a multiplexed RT-LAMP assay for the simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus via the incorporation of fluorescently labelled LAMP probes. Mid-nasal swabs collected from 175 participants on the day of enrolment in the MALCOV Cohort study in Kisumu, Kenya were used in the evaluation of the RT-LAMP assay. Overall, 114 SARS-CoV-2, six Influenza A, two Influenza B and zero RSV samples were identified in the cohort by the Allplex SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB/RSV RT-PCR kit (Seegene Inc) reference test, in addition to 53 negatives. Sensitivity and specificity of the RT-LAMP assay (SARS-CoV-2/FluA/RSV) when compared to RT-PCR was 82.64% [CI95%:74.70-88.92%] and 100% [CI95%:93.40-100%] at 40 minutes for all samples respectively. The mean time to a positive result was 11minutes, highlighting the speed of this technology compared to the more commonly used RT-PCR. RT-LAMP enables rapid multi-pathogen detection with comparable diagnostic accuracy to RT-PCR.

after.authors: Costa, G. P. A.; Gueorguieva, R.; Riggs, M. M.; Dunlap, T.; Sofuoglu, M.; De Aquino, J. P.
after.abstract: Cannabis use is rising fastest among older adults in the U.S., and pain is among the most common reasons they use it. No trial, however, has measured the trade-off between the analgesic and abuse-related effects of {Delta}9-tetrahydrocannabinol ({Delta}9-THC) in this population. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 20 adults aged 65 and older were assigned to oral {Delta}9-THC (placebo, 5, 10 mg) or vaporized {Delta}9-THC (placebo, 2, 4 mg) across three eight-hour sessions in counterbalanced order. We assessed laboratory-evoked pain sensitivity using quantitative sensory testing, abuse liability using subjective drug effects and reinforcement value, and also sampled plasma {Delta}9-THC and 11-OH-THC. Analgesia and abuse liability outcomes were measured repeatedly within each session. On a pain sensitivity index, oral 5 mg relieved pain relative to placebo (p=.040), although the oral arm's overall dose effect was not significant (p=.108); oral 10 mg and both vaporized doses did not differ from placebo. Subjective effects increased with dose and were greatest after vaporization, whereas reinforcement value increased only after vaporized 4 mg. After oral 5 mg, analgesia exceeded placebo at every assessment (60-360 min), while its pleasurable effects peaked at 150 min. Vaporized {Delta}9-THC produced pleasurable effects within 30 min but did not significantly change thermal pain sensitivity. While abuse liability tracked {Delta}9-THC exposure, analgesia showed no significant association, and all adverse events occurred at vaporized 4 mg. These findings suggest dose and route selection may help maximize {Delta}9-THC analgesia while minimizing abuse liability, a strategy that warrants evaluation in clinical populations.

after.authors: Smucny, J.; Campbell, E. M.; Pierce, K. M.; Ward, H. B.; Carter, C. S.; Niendam, T. A.; Lesh, T. A.
after.abstract: Background: Despite their high usage rates and associations with risk for psychosis and earlier age of symptom onset, few studies have examined relationships between nicotine and cannabis co-use and symptoms. Here we examined associations between symptom burden and cannabis/nicotine use/co-use in individuals with early psychosis (EP). Methods: This cross-sectional, multisite cohort study used data from 738 individuals (mean age 22 years, 62% male) from the Early Psychosis Intervention Network (EPI-NET). Relationships between cannabis and/or nicotine use and frequency (over the prior 30 day period) and Modified Colorado Symptom Index (MCSI) scores were examined using mixed effects models, with site as a random factor and age, sex, and cannabis/nicotine use (none, nicotine only, cannabis only, or both) as fixed factors. Exploratory analyses also examined effects of frequency of use (daily vs. less than daily). Results: 59% of the sample used neither nicotine nor cannabis, 17% only nicotine, 9% only cannabis, and 16% both. Significant effects of use were observed on total MCSI score (F = 6.69, p < .001) driven by greater symptoms in individuals who used both cannabis and nicotine relative to neither, only nicotine, or only cannabis. More frequent use, furthermore, was associated with higher total score. Conclusions: These results suggest that co-use of cannabis and nicotine is associated with greater symptom burden in EP, which may have implications for treatment strategies. Neuropharmacological mechanisms that may underlie this association are discussed.

Conclusions: These results suggest that co-use of cannabis and nicotine is associated with greater symptom burden in EP, which may have implications for treatment strategies. after.abstract: Background: Radical cure for P. vivax and P. ovale malaria using 8-aminoquinoline drugs primaquine or tafenoquine can prevent relapse, but requires glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) screening due to the risk of haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals. This study aimed to provide an evidence-based framework to inform the optimal allocation and referral networks for G6PD testing devices in Indonesia. Methods: A diagnostic network optimisation (DNO) analysis using OptiDx was conducted across eight districts in Sumba, North Sumatra, and Central Java, representing high-, moderate-, and low-transmission settings. The maximum annual number of malaria cases from surveillance data between 2019 and 2022 was used as a proxy for testing demand. In baseline scenario, all public health facilities were equipped with G6PD testing devices. In referral scenario, devices were allocated only to selected facilities, with a maximum sample transport distance of 15 kilometres and sample delivery scheduled three times per week. Model outputs were reviewed with the National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP) to identify the optimal scenario, considering factors including implementation cost and accessibility. Results: Equipping 39% (30/76) of facilities in Sumba with G6PD testing devices could reduce total costs by nearly 30% in the first year and approximately 20% in subsequent years compared with the baseline, although the average referral distance increased from 4.48 kilometres to 9.8 kilometres. In North Sumatra, deploying 15 of 68 devices (19%) could reduce total costs by almost 60% in the first year and approximately 15% thereafter. Two health facilities (Puskesmas Padewatu in Sumba and Abdul Manan Hospital in North Sumatra) could experience workload increase exceeding 400 hours annually as referral facilities. In Purworejo, a single device placed at Puskesmas Mranti could enable on-site diagnosis for 56% of patients. Interpretation: The findings demonstrated that DNO can identify cost-efficient and equitable G6PD testing strategies to support safe radical cure and accelerate malaria elimination.

after.abstract: Objective: We aimed to 1) evaluate whether AI algorithms could identify a very low-risk sub-population Lung-RADS 1/2 cases suitable for a safe switch to biennial screening, and 2) externally validate Sybil, an imaging-based deep learning lung cancer risk prediction tool. Materials and methods: We gathered all lung cancer screenings (LCSs) from a tertiary safety-net hospital (n=3120, up to September 2024), manually extracted relevant clinical data, and analyzed Sybil's performance across various subgroups, with a specific focus on Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases. We simulated LCS interval extension using Sybil and the Brock model risk scores calibrated on a subset of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). Confidence intervals were obtained through bootstrapping. Results: The median follow-up was 2.3 years (interquartile range 1.5-3.1), with a total 6-year cancer incidence rate of 2.3% (72/3120). Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases comprised 90.5% of our scans. Sybil's overall area under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.819 to 0.912; while its 2-year AUC for Lung-RADS 1 and 2 cases was 0.746. In the screening interval extension simulation, calibrating for a 30% shift to biennial screening translated into 33.8% of negative screens in our data being safely extended using Sybil, with no delayed cancers. The Brock model demonstrated an AUC of 0.513 on our data, with a sensitivity of 18.2% using the 1.5% threshold. Conclusion: Sybil has the potential to safely extend LCS intervals for low-risk individuals, reducing radiology workload and opening spots for life-saving new screenings.

after.authors: Bellisle, R. F.; McGrath, E.; Waddington, G.; Petersen, L.; Newman, D.
after.abstract: Astronauts experience sensorimotor dysfunction due to microgravity-induced adaptations, leading to impaired posture, locomotion, and manual control. This manuscript details a portable sensorimotor assessment system, including an ankle proprioception test and visual-vestibular tests in a virtual reality headset, which was successfully deployed as a technology demonstration for one astronaut participant pre- and post-spaceflight. Post-flight testing occurred 1 and 3 days after return to Earth (R+1, R+3), with ankle proprioception also tested at R+0. Compared to pre-flight, left ankle proprioception was decreased at R+0 (two standard deviations below the mean of normative data) and returned to pre-flight levels by R+1. All visual-vestibular parameters showed decreased performance post-flight (below the 25th percentile of normative data) and little recovery by R+3. While future validation is required, these assessments appear sensitive to post-flight sensorimotor deconditioning. Furthermore, this technology demonstration highlights the logistical considerations and operational compatibility of the assessments post-flight.

after.title: Preprint: Career development awards are associated with lower career-long research attrition risk in Veterans Affairs investigators.
after.authors: Fraser, J. J.; Hack, S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Office of Research & Development, US Department of Veterans Affairs
after.abstract: Objective:To investigate research attrition and the associated factors among US Department of Veterans Affairs investigators with and without a prior Career Development Award (CDA) from fiscal year 2008 to 2026. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Methods: Investigators whose CDA ended between October 2008 and March 2026 were identified from the Research Analysis and Forecasting Tool (RAFT) database and compared to non-CDA peers. Extracted descriptive variables included sex, investigator type, doctoral degree, salary source, specialty, and research area. Attrition, derived from the electronic Project Management and Information System, was defined when an investigator ceased serving as a principal or coinvestigator on VA-funded research. Analysis utilized attrition percentages, crude count ratios (CR), chi-squared statistics, and multivariable binomial regression to assess adjusted odds ratios (ORadj). Results: Investigators with a prior CDA were 42% less likely to attrite from VA research engagement compared to non-CDA counterparts (CR 95% CI, 0.50-0.67, p<.001). They maintained high engagement regardless of demographic or professional variables (engagement ranges: 66.7%-93.8%). Clinician-scientists were 34% less likely to attrite from science (ORadj 0.54) compared to non-clinician scientists. The 1.68-times higher crude attrition risk for non-VA salaried investigators became non-significant after adjusting for other factors. Attrition was significantly higher in basic science and engineering (ORadj 3.90), endocrinology, metabolism, and nutrition (ORadj 4.24), infectious disease (ORadj 3.80), aging and geriatrics (ORadj 3.56), and cardiopulmonary and vascular research (ORadj 2.70) compared to health services and epidemiology. Conclusion: Prior CDA recipients demonstrate significantly lower research attrition in VA research.

after.title: Preprint: A Reproducible Decomposed Large Language Model Pipeline for Structured Abstraction of Multimodal Neuroimaging Reports: Development and Independent Validation in 1,669 Emergency Department Encounters for Dizziness and Vertigo
after.authors: Shahani, J.; Ousta, A. R.; Shaulov, S.; El-Sherif, Y.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, Staten Island University Hospital, Northwell Health, Staten Island, NY, USA; Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell, Hempstead,
after.abstract: Objective: To develop and independently validate a decomposed, modality-specific large language model (LLM) pipeline that abstracts structured variables from the free-text neuroimaging reports of a multimodal stroke workup, and to validate the resulting structured dataset for reuse in downstream research. Materials and Methods: A frozen pipeline (temperature 0) extracting 22 variables across CT head, CT angiography, CT perfusion, and MRI brain was applied to 1,669 ED encounters for dizziness or vertigo; 11 variables were pre-specified as primary (Tier 1). Reproducibility used three same-session runs and a nine-week repeat run; three frontier models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.5 Flash) measured cross-model agreement (Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa). Accuracy was assessed in an independent 200-encounter cohort (150 random, 50 enriched for rare findings); 100 were double-read by two blinded reviewers with discordances adjudicated. Results: Test-retest reproducibility was high (Tier 1 Fleiss' kappa = 0.993; 99.8% exact) and stable nine weeks later (kappa = 0.992); inter-model agreement was kappa = 0.962. Against the adjudicated reference, pooled Tier 1 accuracy was 0.971 to 0.988 across models (Cohen's kappa 0.959 to 0.982), comparable to inter-reviewer agreement (kappa = 0.932). Accuracy was 0.980 to 0.983 in random and 0.955 to 0.977 in enriched encounters (agreement on model-flagged findings, not sensitivity). Discussion: A decomposed LLM pipeline produced reproducible, model-portable, stable, and accurate multimodal abstraction. Because schema design and validation are up-front costs, such pipelines scale to larger research cohorts. Conclusion: The quantified per-field error rates support reuse of this dataset with field-specific review, and such pipelines offer a practical path to large-scale, reproducible research datasets.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Nutrition, College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Texas A&M University, College Station, Texas, USA; Department of Surgery, Houston Methodist H
after.abstract: Purpose: Interpreting treatment effect size is essential for evidence-informed dietetic care, yet understanding of this competency among dietitians remains unestablished. Methods: We conducted a web-based cross-sectional survey of Australian dietitians (October 2024-February 2025). The survey assessed their understanding of effect size, presented using three absolute estimates (risk difference [RD], risk in treatment vs risk in control groups, number needed to treat [NNT]) and two relative estimates (relative risk [RR], odds ratio [OR]). We also assessed their confidence in determining correct effect size, their perceived usefulness of effect estimates and corresponding certainty of evidence. Results: Approximately 7697 dietitians received the survey link. 27 participated and 13 completers were analyzed. Correct understanding was higher for absolute than relative estimates (30.0% vs 18.2%). Risk in treatment vs risk in control groups was understood the most (41.7%) and RD, RR and OR the least (18.2% each). Confidence was highest for RR [mean (SD): 4.18 (1.25)] and lowest for NNT [3.40 (1.17)]. Perceived usefulness was highest for OR [4.69 (1.18)] and lowest for NNT [3.75 (1.76)]. Certainty of evidence was rated useful [5.69 (1.03)]. Conclusion: Based on a small sample, preliminary evidence suggests limited understanding of effect size among Australian dietitians, highlighting the need for further training and assessment in larger sample.

after.authors: Sunuwar, D. R.; Shrestha, A.; Kiwanayo, A.; Karki, S.; Shrestha, M.; Sunuwar, S.; Singh, D. R.; Karki, K.; Chaudhary, N. K.; K.C., D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Public Health Promotion and Development Organization
after.abstract: Background The double burden of malnutrition (DBM), characterised by coexisting undernutrition and overnutrition, remains a public health concern among adolescents especially in low- and middle-income countries. Adolescents in Nepal are nutritionally vulnerable, yet evidence on the coexistence of stunting and overweight/obesity is limited. This study assessed the prevalence and associated factors of DBM among school-going adolescents in urban Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. Methods A school-based cross-sectional study was conducted to assess factors associated with the double burden of malnutrition among adolescents in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. A multi-stage cluster random sampling technique, using the Probability Proportional to Size method, was employed to ensure the selection of the desired number of participants. Students from grades 8 to 10 were randomly selected for face-to-face interviews and anthropometric measurements (height and weight were collected to calculate Body Mass Index (BMI)-for-age Z-scores (BAZ)), using tools adapted to the local context. Bivariate and multivariable models examined the associations between the dependent and independent variables. Results This study revealed that 15.3% of the students were stunted, 5.5% were underweight, 16.9% were overweight/obese, and 3% of students with the coexistence of DBM. In the fully adjusted model, the odds of stunting were significantly higher among adolescents aged 15-19 years (aOR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.35-3.06), salty-snack consumers (aOR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.00-2.36), those with low nutritional knowledge (aOR = 3.17, 95% CI: 2.17-4.66), and low diet quality (aOR = 7.27, 95% CI: 4.96-10.65). Conversely, fatty-food consumption was associated with lower odds of stunting (aOR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.42-1.00). For overweight/obesity, older adolescents had significantly lower odds (aOR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.35-0.67). Regarding the double burden of malnutrition (DBM), low nutritional knowledge (aOR = 2.16, 95% CI: 0.99-4.71) and low diet quality (aOR = 5.27, 95% CI: 2.42-11.48) were significantly associated with higher odds. Conclusion The double burden of malnutrition exists among adolescents in urban Kathmandu Valley, highlighting a critical public health challenge. Socio-demographic, dietary, and behavioral factors significantly influence its prevalence. Comprehensive school- and community-based interventions are crucial for addressing this dual nutritional burden.

Socio-demographic, dietary, and behavioral factors significantly influence its prevalence. Comprehensive school- and community-based interventions are crucial for addressing this dual nutritional burden.

after.title: Preprint: A population-based resource for the prioritization of rare variants of unknown significance in clinical genomics
after.authors: Tremblay, S.; Moreau, C.; Morin, G.-P.; Laprise, C.; Girard, S. L.
after.abstract: Rare diseases represent a major public health challenge because they are often associated with severe phenotypes, yet many causal variants remain undiscovered. Founder populations provide a unique opportunity to identify disease-causing variants through the local enrichment of rare alleles. Using whole-genome sequencing data from individuals in the Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean population, enriched variants were identified and their founder status was assessed through identity-by-descent sharing. Variant impact was evaluated using functional prediction tools without relying on prior clinical classification. A total of 131 founder variants of interest were identified, most of which would likely have been overlooked by conventional approaches based on existing clinical annotations. We developed a web-based platform that facilitates clinician access to the latest interpretation of their genetic variants of interest. These findings demonstrate that potentially pathogenic variants can remain undetected even in extensively studied founder populations. More broadly, they highlight the value of population structure-based approaches for uncovering rare disease variants and improving the characterization of genetic disease risk across human populations.

E.; Apriyana, I.; Babiker, H.; Rakotoarivony, R.; Hendershott, M.; Kasina, P.; Kalungi, A.; Ojewunmi, O.; Pascart, T.; Rosso, S.; Verdugo, R. after.abstract: Immune allele frequencies inform disease association mapping, pharmacogenomic guidance, and vaccine design, yet such data are missing for most of the world's groups. Here we present the Global Atlas of Immune Alleles (GAIA), applying benchmarked genotyping tools across the Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA), Immunoglobulin Heavy Chain Constant (IGHC), and Fc Gamma Receptor (FCGR) loci to whole-genome sequencing data from 20,248 individuals, oversampling sub-Saharan African, Island Southeast Asian, and Pacific groups. Despite representing fewer than 0.5% of observations in the Allele Frequency Net Database, GAIA expands the database's catalogue by 38%, demonstrating that representation matters more than sample size. We identify HLA alleles at group-specific frequencies that challenge pharmacogenomic screening recommendations and document disease-risk alleles common in groups lacking clinical guidance. Finally, we introduce majority allelic diversity (MAD-X), which counts the alleles required for X% of individuals in a group to carry at least one, and show that reaching 90% HLA-B coverage for vaccine design requires up to 2.7 times more alleles in underrepresented groups than in those of Northwest European ancestry.

after.abstract: Medicaid is a government program providing benefits to 1 in 5 people in the US, including medical care for children and adults, long-term care for the elderly, and home/community-based services for the disabled[1]. Effective January 1st 2027, HR1 (One Big Beautiful Bill) passed by Congress will implement new administrative requirements to Medicaid expected to strip benefits from 1.8 million adults, children, and seniors[2]. As each US state administers Medicaid independently, the timing, frequency, and severity of those losses may vary across states. Monitoring that human impact requires an detailed ongoing view of affected individuals and their families. To monitor the human-impact of HR1, this work develops a proof-of-concept using topic analysis and LLMs to generate detailed categorization of individuals' Medicaid experiences across multiple states and over time.

after.title: Preprint: A Multilevel Framework for Evaluating the Impact of Monoclonal Antibodies Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Daycare and Households
after.authors: Li, K.; Pitzer, V. E.; Weinberger, D.
after.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) reduce the risk of severe disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among immunized infants. The potential of these products to indirectly protect unimmunized contacts remains incompletely understood. This uncertainty is, in part, due to our limited understanding of how mAbs may influence population-level RSV transmission. Here, we develop a multiscale simulation framework that integrates RSV transmission dynamics across households and daycare centers to explore the characteristics of the population that could influence the strength of indirect effects of infant mAb immunization. The framework incorporates individual-level heterogeneity in age and time-varying infectiousness, as well as demographic variation in household composition and contact patterns, to capture realistic transmission pathways across close-contact networks. Using a virtual population informed by U.S. household characteristics, we show that infant immunization would only be expected to provide modest indirect protection to toddlers, and the magnitude of these effects depends on contact structure and intervention coverage. Our findings demonstrate the importance of integrating fine-scale transmission networks into evaluations of RSV prevention strategies and provide a generalizable framework for assessing population-level impacts of interventions against respiratory pathogens.

after.title: Preprint: Clinical and Social Determinants of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Optimization in Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
after.authors: Nelson, M.; Kwon, M.; Driscoll, K.; Kaiwan, O.; Dunlap, M. E.; Murad, K.; Rybinska- Campbel, A.; Gunzler, D. D.; Nandar, P. P.
after.abstract: Background: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is associated with high morbidity and mortality. Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for HFrEF has been shown to improve outcomes, with higher GDMT scores at hospital discharge being associated with lower mortality, fewer rehospitalizations and reduced healthcare costs. Yet, disparities in the utilization of GDMT remain. In this study, we examined the effect of various clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic factors on the utilization of GDMT in HFrEF patients referred to Cardiology in a tertiary care safety net hospital, using a standardized GDMT scoring system. Methods: We conducted a single-center cross-sectional retrospective analysis of patients who had an index HFrEF 40% diagnosis between January 1, 2024, to December 31, 2024, and who were referred to Cardiology at a tertiary care safety net hospital. Baseline characteristics, laboratory investigations, health care utilization, and GDMT score data were extracted at the ambulatory care visit nearest to 90 days from the index HF diagnosis. GDMT score ranges from 0 to 9 factored in doses of beta-blocker (BB), angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker (ACEi/ARB), mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI), isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine (ISDN/HYD). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to examine associations between low GDMT scores (0-4) nearest to 90 days from new onset HFrEF diagnosis and several clinical, demographic, and socioeconomic variables. Results: In 200 patients meeting entry criteria, mean age was 62.7 years, 64.0% were male, 47.5% were classified as white and 42.0% as Black. 39.5% had a low GDTM score (<5). The following were less likely to be associated with low GDMT score: diabetes mellitus (adjusted OR: 0.41, 95%CI=0.18-0.91) and frequent medical appointments (adjusted OR: 0.37, 95% CI=0.25-0.54), while higher serum eGFR was more likely to be associated with low GDMT score (adjusted OR: 1.02, 95%CI=1.00-1.03). There was no significant association between GDMT score and age, sex, race, or payer status. Conclusion: In patients with HFrEF referred to Cardiology in our safety net tertiary care center, higher utilization of GDMT at 90 days was achieved in those who have diabetes mellitus, more frequent medical appointments, or lower serum eGFR. There was no difference in GDMT utilization according to age, sex, race, or payer status predictive of lower GDMT scores. Contrary to findings from previous studies, no significant differences were observed across demographic or payer groups, emphasizing the role of healthcare access and utilization.

after.authors: Hammer, Y.; Cohen, Y. J.; Arbel, R.; Razi, T.; Netzer, D.; Ben Gal, T.; Weinstein, J. M.; Iakobishvili, Z.; Yamin, D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Cardiology Department, Rabin Medical Center, Petah Tikva, Israel; Gray School of Medicine, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv, Israel
after.abstract: Aims: To evaluate the effectiveness of GLP-1 RAs on clinical outcomes in diabetic patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Methods and results: In this retrospective observational cohort study, all adults with diabetes mellitus and HFrEF between 2014 and 2025 were identified. Patients treated with GLP-1 RAs were matched to controls using stratified exact matching. The primary outcome was a composite of heart failure hospitalization or all-cause mortality. Treatment effects were estimated using nonparametric bootstrap resampling (1,000 iterations) to derive risk ratios, NNT estimates, and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Time-to-event analyses using Cox proportional hazards models were performed as a validation analysis. Among 7,878 patients with HFrEF, 793 (10.1%) patients who initiated GLP-1 RA therapy after HF diagnosis were matched to 1,825 controls. GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a lower risk of heart failure hospitalization or death, with risk ratios of 0.58 (95% CI: 0.42-0.77) at 12 months and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.61-0.85) at 36 months. The combination of high baseline event rates and substantial relative risk reduction translated into remarkably low NNT values in the overall population, with an NNT of 17 (95% CI: 11-33) at 1 year and 13 (95% CI: 8-25) at 3 years. Post hoc subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent effects across clinical subgroups, with no significant heterogeneity observed. Conclusion: In this large real-world cohort of diabetic patients with HFrEF, GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy, in addition to guideline-directed medical therapy, was associated with a lower risk of death or heart failure hospitalization.

after.title: Preprint: Periodontitis and Associated Factors Among Dental Outpatients at Tertiary Hospitals in Dhaka
after.authors: Kanta, S. M.; Shama, F. F.; Sharower, M. G.; Sharmin, S.; Sultana, H.
after.abstract: Objective: To identify the factors associated with periodontitis among dental outpatient departments at tertiary hospitals in Dhaka. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 227 patients from dental outpatient departments of three tertiary-level hospitals in Dhaka, Bangladesh by intra-oral examinations and in-person interviews using a pretested semi-structured questionnaire through Simplified Oral Hygiene Index (OHI-S) and the Community Periodontal Index (CPI) component of the CPITN. Results: About 55% were classified as having periodontitis. Both diabetes mellitus (p < 0.05) and harmful oral habits (smoking, smokeless tobacco, and constant tooth picking) were significantly associated with periodontitis (p < 0.05). Participants with diabetes had 2.87 times higher odds of periodontitis (OR: 2.870, 95% CI: 1.516-5.441). The odds of having periodontitis were 7.27 times higher for smokeless tobacco users (OR: 7.271, 95% CI: 3.609-14.651), and smokers had 3.69-fold higher odds of periodontitis (OR: 3.687, 95% CI: 1.701-7.988). A strong positive correlation was observed between poor oral hygiene status and the presence of periodontitis (r = 0.947, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Diabetes, smoking and poor oral hygiene are key determinants of periodontitis which underscore the need for targeted oral health promotion, regular screening and integration of periodontal care into geriatric services. Keywords: Periodontitis; Oral hygiene; Tobacco use; Diabetes mellitus

after.title: Preprint: The origin of the MV Hondius Andes outbreak
after.authors: Ulloa-Zepeda, L.; Parker, E.; Gangavarapu, K.; Castillo, A.; Pavez, C.; Fernandez, J.; Vilches, M.; Vial, P.; Rambaut, A.; Andersen, K. G.; Vial, C.
after.abstract: In April-July 2026, Andes virus (ANDV) caused an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulting in 12 confirmed cases and three deaths. Before symptom onset, the index case had travelled through hantavirus-endemic regions of Chile and Argentina, leaving the geographic origin of infection unresolved. We conducted phylogenetic and phylogeographic analyses using newly generated ANDV genomes from human cases and rodent reservoirs to investigate the likely origin of the outbreak. Through phylogenetic analyses, we show that the outbreak genome falls within a geographically structured lineage spanning southern Chile and Argentine Andean Patagonia. Using phylogeographic reconstructions across all three segments, integrated with the index case's travel itinerary, we identified the Tolten-Lanco area of southern Chile as the most likely geographic origin of the outbreak genome, with two candidate locations accounting for >98% of the posterior support. However, the index case visited this area 62-66 days before symptom onset, exceeding the conventionally reported ANDV incubation period of 7-42 days. Thus, while genomic evidence supports a southern Chilean origin of the outbreak genome, the timing and circumstances of transmission to the index case remain unresolved.

after.title: Preprint: Determinants of Binge Drinking Among Current Alcohol Drinkers: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 2013 Health and Welfare Survey
after.authors: Pongsupatananon, P.; Reangsan, D.
after.abstract: This cross sectional analytical study examined the prevalence and determinants of binge drinking (BD) among current alcohol drinkers (CAD) aged 20 years and older in Thailand (N = 52,847). Data from the Health and Welfare Surveys (HWS) were analyzed using chi square tests and multiple logistic regression. In 2013, nearly 69% of the 5,445 current drinkers reported BD. Multivariable analyses indicated significantly higher odds of BD among men (AOR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.90-2.66; p < 0.001), younger adults (AOR range: 1.50-1.90; p < 0.001), individuals with household housing expenses (AOR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.01-1.39; p < 0.05), and those with secondary/vocational or tertiary education (AOR range: 1.35-1.36; p < 0.05). Smoking was also associated with elevated odds of BD (AOR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.23-1.62; p < 0.001). In contrast, respondents in high income groups had lower odds (AOR = 0.69, 95% CI: 0.54-0.87; p < 0.01), as did residents of non metropolitan areas compared with Bangkok (AOR range: 0.44-0.59; p < 0.01). In conclusion, binge drinking affected over half of Thai drinkers and was strongly linked to demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and behavioral factors. The frequent co-occurrence of alcohol use and smoking underscores the clustering of non-communicable disease risks, highlighting the need for integrated dual-cessation programs. While cross-sectional design and 2013 data limitations apply, these findings provide actionable evidence for public health agencies to implement targeted screening and intervention strategies for high-risk populations.

after.title: Preprint: Spatial distribution and factors associated with unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia: Evidence from the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey
after.authors: Sibeso, P.; Tembo, N.; Jacobs, C.
after.abstract: Unmet need for family planning contributes to unintended pregnancies, unsafe abortions, and preventable maternal and child deaths, and remains high in sub-Saharan Africa. In Zambia, national estimates may conceal important geographic inequalities. We assessed the spatial distribution of, and factors associated with, unmet need for family planning among women of reproductive age in Zambia. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS), including 12,133 women aged 15-49 years. Survey-weighted logistic regression, accounting for the stratified two-stage cluster design, was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Global spatial autocorrelation was assessed with Morans I, local hotspots with the Getis-Ord Gi* statistic, and spatial clusters with a purely spatial Bernoulli scan statistic in SaTScan. The weighted prevalence of unmet need was 27.0% (95% CI: 25.7-28.3%), ranging from 23.8% in Central to 31.6% in North-Western Province. Unmet need was spatially clustered (Morans I = 0.142, p = 0.018), with hotspots mainly in Lusaka, Southern, North-Western, and Northern provinces; SaTScan detected a primary cluster in Lusaka (observed-to-expected ratio 1.42, p < 0.001). Women in union (AOR 2.33, 95% CI: 1.90-2.86) and never-married women (AOR 2.20, 95% CI: 1.69-2.86) had higher odds of unmet need than formerly married women, as did women with five or more children compared with none (AOR 3.05, 95% CI: 2.25-4.13). Lower odds were observed among women aged 35-49 years (AOR 0.65, 95% CI: 0.52-0.83), women in the richest wealth quintile (AOR 0.62, 95% CI: 0.45-0.86), employed women (AOR 0.73, 95% CI: 0.64-0.84) and urban residents (AOR 0.80, 95% CI: 0.68-0.95). Unmet need for family planning in Zambia is high, geographically clustered and socially patterned. Family planning programmes should prioritise hotspot areas, particularly Lusaka, Southern and North-Western provinces, while targeting younger, higher-parity and poorer women.

after.title: Preprint: Biomarkers of ageing and lung function trajectory: a multi-omics study in a UK birth cohort
after.authors: Grenville, J. S.; Yousefi, P. D.; Power, G. M.; Richmond, R. C.; Dodd, J. W.
after.abstract: BACKGROUND: Accelerated biological ageing and cellular senescence are pathogenically implicated in COPD and may represent therapeutic targets. Adverse early-life lung function trajectories offer opportunities to prevent COPD but their relationship with epigenetic and proteomic ageing biomarkers remains unexplored. We investigated using conventional epidemiological and Mendelian randomisation (MR) methods. METHODS: Outcomes were the two lowest of five FEV1 trajectories (Persistently Low and Below Average) previously identified using latent profile analysis (ages 8-30) in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children. Exposures included nine measures of blood-derived epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and thirteen senescence-associated plasma proteins (ages 7-9). We used logistic regression to estimate odds of lower trajectory membership by exposure and bidirectional one-sample MR to investigate causation. RESULTS: Higher plasma CXCL10 (OR 1.29 per SD; 95% CI 1.03, 1.57), IL6 (OR 1.29; 1.03, 1.57) and IL33 (OR 1.23; 1.04, 1.44) were associated with Persistently Low lung function trajectory, with little evidence for associations between EAA and lower trajectories. MR provided little evidence that genetically predicted plasma proteins influenced risk of lower trajectories, but lower genetically proxied childhood FEV1 predicted higher plasma CXCL10 at ages 9 ({beta} -0.34; -0.65, -0.03) and 24 ({beta} -0.38; -0.67, -0.08). INTERPRETATION: Childhood plasma CXCL10, IL6 and IL33, but not EAA, predict low lung function trajectory into early adulthood. Lower childhood lung function may causally relate to persistently increased plasma CXCL10. Future research should investigate IL33 as a potential therapeutic target in low lung function trajectory and persistent systemic inflammation as a mechanism for associated multimorbidity.

after.title: Preprint: Symptom variability and treatment response in pernicious anaemia: a longitudinal daily symptom tracking study
after.authors: Thain, A.; Hart, K.; Burchell, K.; Visser, P.; Ahmadi, K. R.
after.abstract: Pernicious Anaemia is an autoimmune-mediated disorder of vitamin B12 absorption, managed using fixed-interval vitamin B12 replacement regimens. Despite treatment, many patients report persistent or recurrent symptoms, suggesting substantial inter-individual variability in treatment response. More tailored approaches may therefore be needed to reduce symptom burden and improve quality of life. This prospective observational study used high-frequency longitudinal digital symptom monitoring to characterise symptom dynamics and heterogeneity in treatment response. UK adults with pernicious anaemia, recruited via the Pernicious Anaemia Society, self-reported daily symptoms (severity 0-10) and vitamin B12 treatments over three months. Analyses quantified within- and between-person variability, injection-aligned symptom response kinetics, and differences in treatment response by injection frequency. Sixty-eight participants were included in the longitudinal analyses, providing >5,100 person-days of symptom data over a mean of 76 days (SD 28). Most symptom variance was attributable to stable between-person differences (ICC range, 0.58-0.80), indicating the persistence of individual symptom phenotypes. Vitamin B12 injections were followed by rapid symptom improvement, although magnitude and timing varied markedly by symptom domain. Seventy-one percent of participants were classified as responders for composite symptom burden (median 4.65 to 2.36; p<0.001), while 29% showed no meaningful multisystem improvement (3.59 to 3.58; p=0.63). Cognitive symptoms improved earliest, typically within 24-72 hours; fatigue and pain responses peaked at 3-5 days, and neuro-sensory symptoms at 4-6 days. Responses clustered within individuals, indicating distinct responder phenotypes. Overall symptom burden improved most among participants receiving monthly injections, whereas those injecting weekly or more often had higher pre-injection burden and smaller improvements. These findings suggest that fixed-interval vitamin B12 replacement may not adequately reflect individual variation in symptom recurrence and treatment response. High-frequency digital symptom monitoring may provide a practical framework for characterising these patterns and for evaluating more individualised, symptom-guided vitamin B12 management.

after.title: Preprint: Modulating Amygdala Responses in Major Depressive Disorder using Naturalistic Neurofeedback with Emotional Faces
after.authors: Lor, C. S.; Haugg, A.; Langer, M.; Willinger, D.; Aubry, J.; Molinari, K.; Staempfli, P.; Zhang, M.; Kleim, B.; Bruehl, A.; Sladky, R.; Scharnowski, F.; Watve, A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Zurich Center for Neuroeconomics, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland; Department of Cognition, Emotion, and Methods in Psychology, Faculty of Psychology,
after.abstract: Emotion regulation is critical to mental health, and its disruption can lead to psychiatric conditions such as major depressive disorder (MDD). MDD encompasses diverse symptoms, including anhedonia and anxiety, which may be associated with distinct patterns of altered neural activity. Interventions that address the neural mechanisms underlying these symptom dimensions may improve treatment efficacy. We investigated an adaptive, naturalistic real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging neurofeedback paradigm designed to differentially target anhedonia and anxiety through bidirectional amygdala regulation. Unlike conventional abstract feedback, our approach used emotional faces whose expressions changed dynamically according to ongoing amygdala activity, embedding neural self-regulation within a socially relevant emotional context. In this parallel-group study, 21 patients with MDD received one of two neurofeedback conditions. In the Happy-up group, patients attempted to increase amygdala activity by making a neutral face happier to enhance positive emotional responding. In the Fear-down group, patients attempted to decrease amygdala activity by making a fearful face less fearful to reduce negative emotional reactivity. Both groups showed the expected pattern of neural regulation during neurofeedback, with greater amygdala activity during Happy upregulation and decreasing amygdala activity during Fear downregulation. Following the intervention, patients showed reductions in depression severity, anxiety, and anhedonia, and more positive evaluations of neutral and happy faces. However, improvements in anhedonia and anxiety did not differ significantly between groups. These findings show bidirectional amygdala regulation through naturalistic neurofeedback in MDD. Although symptom-specific clinical effects were not established, the observed clinical improvements underscore the therapeutic potential of this approach.

after.title: Preprint: Knowledge, attitudes and behaviours related to tick awareness and prevention among users of urban green spaces: insights from stakeholder focus groups
after.authors: Taylor-Egbeyemi, J. L.; Masterton, S.; Robin, C.
after.abstract: Abstract Background: Ticks in the UK can transmit pathogens that lead to diseases in humans, including Lyme disease and tick-borne encephalitis. Expanding tick populations and increasing human use of urban green spaces may elevate exposure risk. Public health advice exists, but little is known about how this guidance is understood and applied by users of urban environments. Methods: Four stakeholder focus groups were conducted with professionals involved in tick fieldwork in urban green spaces. Discussions explored interactions with the public, perceived awareness, behaviours, and views on communication. Data were analysed thematically using an approach informed by the Framework Method. Results: Stakeholders reported substantial variation in public awareness of ticks, influenced by prior exposure to rural environments and local knowledge. Misinformation, particularly around tick removal, was common. Signage was rarely observed in urban green spaces, and views on its effectiveness were mixed. Participants emphasised the need to balance risk communication with reassurance and highlighted the importance of age-appropriate education. Conclusions: Insights from stakeholders underline the importance of targeted, context specific public health messaging in urban settings. Priorities include identifying groups with lower awareness, addressing misinformation, designing balanced communication materials, evaluating the effectiveness of signage, and integrating education for children and families.

after.title: Preprint: From telling to receiving: the disclosure-and-services cascade after childhood sexual abuse across 15 low- and middle-income countries
after.authors: Sood, S.; Malhotra, G.; Ramaiya, A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg School of Public Health
after.abstract: Most children who experience sexual abuse in low- and middle-income countries never receive formal help, but few studies have followed survivors through the steps from telling someone to receiving services. In this pooled cross-sectional analysis, we combined 15 nationally representative Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS) fielded between 2013 and 2024 in sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, and Eastern Europe to describe this disclosure-and-services cascade and the factors associated with each step. The analytic sample comprised 3,608 respondents aged 18-24 years who reported sexual abuse before age 18 (2,852 female, 756 male). We estimated survey-weighted proportions for four steps: told anyone, knew where to seek formal help, sought help (among those who knew), and received help (among those who sought it). Design-based logistic regression with country fixed effects estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for individual, family, and community factors. Overall, 47.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 44.4-49.7) of survivors had told anyone and 34.8% (32.2-37.5) knew where to seek formal help. Of those who knew (n = 1,208), 24.8% (20.9-29.1) sought help, and of those who sought help (n = 339), 81.9% (75.9-86.7) received it. In total, 7.0% (5.7-8.5) of survivors received formal help; this proportion ranged from 0.9% to 26.3% across countries. Compared with male survivors, female survivors were more likely to tell anyone (aOR 2.30, 95% CI 1.73-3.05) and less likely to know where to seek help (aOR 0.68, 0.50-0.93); among survivors who knew where to go, female survivors were more likely to seek help (aOR 2.66, 1.39-5.09). Knowing where to seek help was more likely with older age, more schooling, and a living mother. Survivors who had ever married or cohabited were less likely to have told anyone (aOR 0.75, 0.58-0.96). No factor other than sex was associated with seeking help among those who knew where to go. Most survivors are lost before they reach a service: two in three do not know where to go, and three in four of those who know ultimately do not seek help. Once survivors seek help, most receive it. Interventions should make services known to young people, particularly those with less schooling, and address the barriers that keep survivors, especially young men, from using services they know about.

after.authors: Mathis, S. M.; Borchering, R.; Susswein, Z.; McIntosh, N.; Corbett, P.; Carey, K.; Couture, A.; Kniss, K.; Reinhart, K.; Hawkins, D.; Connolly, S.; Richard, D.; Howes, A.; Budd, A.; Gostic, K.; Biggerstaff, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
after.abstract: CDC has estimated the time-varying reproduction number (Rt) for influenza in the United States since 2023, translating the posterior probability that Rt exceeds one, P(R_t>1), into epidemic trend categories (growing, likely growing, not changing, likely declining, declining). If Rt reliably indicates infection dynamics, growing or declining trends should precede corresponding changes in influenza-related emergency department (ED) visits, accounting for the lag between infection and care-seeking. However, because these categories reflect confidence in the direction of change rather than magnitude, their alignment with the corresponding trends ED activity measures is unclear. We compared weekly Rt epidemic trend categories to observed ED trends from the National Syndromic Surveillance Program across the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza seasons, using three thresholds to define observed trends at different magnitudes ([≥]0.1% difference, [≥]0.5% difference, [≥]5% relative change between consecutive weeks), comparing Rt trends to observed trends the following week. We assessed categorical alignment and calibration between P(R_t>1) and observed trends. Alignment was moderate overall, strongest for growing and declining categories under the 5% relative change threshold (61% aligned) and weakest under the 0.5% difference threshold (38.2% aligned); calibration was similarly best under the 5% relative change threshold. Misalignment concentrated around epidemic inflection points and periods of low influenza activity. Rt epidemic trend categories showed moderate, threshold-dependent alignment with observed ED activity, reflecting a combination of real-time model error and misalignment between direction-based and magnitude-based surveillance metrics. Defining categories based on Rt magnitude could improve correspondence with size-based change indicators and strengthen their utility for real-time monitoring.

after.title: Preprint: Effects of Weighted Seated Core Exercises on Immediate Postural Stability in Healthy Young Adults: An Exploratory Study
after.authors: Fujino, F.; Yamakawa, M.; Kono, T.; Higaki, T.; Maeda, K.
after.abstract: Objectives: This exploratory study investigated whether low-load, seated core exercises could produce immediate improvements in standing balance among healthy young adults, aiming to provide a foundation for safe, early-stage rehabilitation protocols. Methods: Ten healthy males performed seated core exercises consisted of alternating hip flexion 5 times per side while seated and maintaining bilateral shoulder flexion at 120-degree shoulder flexion under four load conditions: upper-limb weight only, a 400-g empty box, a 1-kg ball, and a 2-kg ball. Immediately following the exercise, participants performed a 10-s single-leg stance. Transversus abdominis (TrA) thickness was measured via wireless ultrasound at baseline, post-exercise, and during the stance. Center of pressure (CoP) sway was recorded concurrently to evaluate postural stability. Results: Left-side TrA thickness during stance increased significantly under the 1-kg and 2-kg load conditions compared to baseline (p < 0.05), although substantial missing data for the left-side measurements limited the robustness of this finding. No significant load-dependent effects were observed for CoP sway parameters (p > 0.05). A moderate positive correlation (rho = 0.43, p = 0.002) was found between right-side TrA thickness and CoP sway velocity during the single-leg stance. Conclusions: Low-load, seated core exercises do not yield immediate enhancements in standing stability in healthy populations. The results suggest that increased TrA thickness during a balance task may correlate with heightened postural instability rather than improved balance control. Further research is needed to determine whether these findings translate to clinical populations with impaired physical fitness.

after.title: Preprint: Cross-reactive antibody and functional T-cell responses to Bundibugyo virus induced by Zaire ebolavirus vaccination and infection
after.authors: Wiedemann, A.; Ayouba, A.; Lhomme, E.; Foucat, E.; Kisrani, S.; Thaurignac, G.; Ben-Farhat, S.; Postebogui Study group,  ; PREVAC study team,  ; Peeters, M.; Levy, Y.
after.abstract: Background There is no licensed specific vaccine against the current Ebola Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbeak affecting the Democratic Republic of the Congo. However, clinical evaluations of a licensed Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) vaccine have just launched. It remains unclear whether EBOV infection or vaccination generate cross-reactive immunity against BDBV. Methods We quantified CD4 and CD8 T-cell magnitude, polyfunctionality, and cytotoxicity after 8-day expansion with EBOV, BDBV, Sudan (SUDV), or Marburg (MARV) GP peptide pools, and measured GP-binding antibodies by multiplex assay, in recipients of Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo (n=10), single-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (n=10), or two-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (n=8) (NCT02876328), and in EVD survivors sampled approximately 3 years after infection (n=10). Findings Fourteen days after completion of each licensed vaccine regimen, median BDBV-reactive CD4 responses were 9.8% [IQR:8.9-14.0] after single-dose rVSVG-ZEBOV-GP (D14) and 8.0% [5.5-9.9] after Ad26.ZEBOV/MVA-BN-Filo (D70). The highest BDBV-reactive CD8response was observed in survivors (24.7% [20.3-33.1]), together with a prominent cytotoxic CD8 response (14.4% [10.4-19.7]) ; corresponding vaccine-group medians ranged from 0.9% to 17.7% and from 0.6% to 6.7%, respectively. SUDV responses were also detected, whereas MARV recognition was limited. BDBV-binding antibodies were detected following both vaccine regimens, with the highest levels observed in survivors (491 [330-1261] net MFI). Among vaccinees, EBOV- and BDBV-reactive cellular and humoral responses were positively correlated after adjustment for multiple testing. Interpretation EBOV infection and vaccination elicited BDBV-cross-reactive T-cell responses and binding antibodies. These findings support further evaluation of existing EBOV vaccines in the context of BDBV outbreaks. Funding INSERM, Vaccine Research Institute (ANR-10-LABX-77-01), and Institut de Recherche pour le Developpement (IRD).

after.title: Preprint: Effect of protocolized MAGNesium replacement in critically ill patients On mortaLIty and Atrial fibrillation: protocol for the MAGNOLIA randomized controlled trial
after.authors: Yarnell, C. J.; Bruce-Kemevor, S.; Burns, K.; Burry, L.; Craig, J.; Fernando, S. M.; Fowler, R.; Gunaratne, K.; Haskings, J.; Lamontagne, F.; Liu, K.; Prakash, V.; Sibley, S.; Soliman, K.; Tomlinson, G.; Wei, L.; Bodley, T.; Canadian Critical Care Trials Group,
after.category: intensive care and critical care medicine
after.abstract: Background: Measurement of serum magnesium levels, and administration of supplemental magnesium when levels are below target, is a common element of routine care for critically ill patients. However, targets for replacement vary, and the targets that lead to the best outcomes are unknown. Methods: Multi-center open-label parallel group randomized controlled superiority trial of adult critically ill patients receiving protocolized magnesium replacement, comparing a higher target (>0.95mmol/L) to a lower target (>0.7mmol/L). The trial will be embedded into the electronic health record (EHR) at 6 hospitals across 2 health networks in Ontario, Canada, with a shared EHR. We will include patients aged 16 years or older who have ICU admission orders, including an order for the magnesium replacement protocol. Patients with pre-eclampsia, sustained ventricular tachycardia, or neuromuscular junction disease will be excluded. Because both targets lie within the standard of care, we will use an opt-out consent approach. Screening will be integrated with the EHR, such that when a patient meets inclusion criteria, a pop-up will appear to allow the ordering clinician to confirm eligibility or indicate the relevant exclusion. After the clinician confirms eligibility, patients will be randomly assigned to a magnesium target. The primary outcome will be an ordinal composite, evaluated at 30 days, composed of death and the number of days free of atrial fibrillation or flutter in ICU. Secondary outcomes will include ventricular arrhythmia and antiarrhythmics administered; receipt of vasopressors, ventilation, and new renal replacement therapy in ICU; lengths of ICU and hospital stay; hospital mortality at 60 and 90 days, magnesium levels, and magnesium supplementation. For analyses, we will use Bayesian regression with weakly skeptical priors and an intention-to-treat approach. Outcome ascertainment will occur within the EHR. Discussion: This randomized controlled trial addresses an important uncertainty regarding routine care in the ICU with an EHR-embedded design. The innovative EHR-embedded design facilitates the large sample sizes and comprehensive, equitable recruitment needed for a trial evaluating a routine care intervention, and will lead to seamless integration with routine care upon trial completion. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07173855. Registered 12 September 2025, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07173855.

after.title: Preprint: Consumer continuous glucose monitoring uncovers hidden metabolic risk in free-living adults without diabetes
after.authors: Ginart, P.; Loesche, M. A.
after.abstract: Whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides actionable information in adults without diabetes is contested, as its metrics were designed for diabetes and screening relies on HbA1c. In this cross-sectional study of 62,122 free-living adults on the Levels digital-health platform, average glucose was the most reliable measure across weeks (intraclass correlation 0.747). Among 7,930 participants without diabetes with laboratory data, it tracked insulin resistance, triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, uric acid, and C-reactive protein more closely than HbA1c, explaining nearly three times more variance in fasting insulin (R2 0.131 vs 0.048). With a normal HbA1c, occult hyperinsulinemia (fasting insulin [≥]10 {micro}IU/mL) was twice as common at average glucose [≥]110 mg/dL (27.5% vs 12.6%). Counterintuitively, at the same average glucose, spike width, not height or frequency, tracked insulin resistance, triglycerides, and C-reactive protein; carbohydrate sensitivity, although reliable, did not track insulin resistance. This analysis suggests a framework for interpreting CGM in adults without diabetes.

after.authors: Gustani-Buss, E.; Weinberger, D. M.; Grubaugh, N. D.; Colizza, V.; Shao, Y.; Suchard, M.; Evers, A.; Mazur, N. I.; Wildenbeest, J. G.; Lebbink, R. J.; Zoggel, H. J. A. A. v.; Bont, L.; Lemey, P.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Pediatric Infectious Diseases and Immunology, University Medical Center Utrecht, Utrecht, The Netherlands.
after.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic dramatically disrupted the seasonal circulation of RSV, with subsequent heterogeneous global resurgence. We aimed to characterize how pandemic-era disruptions restructured global RSV transmission dynamics, evolutionary patterns, and drivers of reemergence. We show that RSV-A and RSV-B genetic diversity underwent profound pandemic-associated suppression followed by heterogeneous resurgence. The post-pandemic period was characterized by pronounced changes in diversity, with the emergence of novel RSV-A genotypes (A.D.3 and A.D.5.2) and the expansion of the RSV-B, B.D.E.1 genotype. The recovery of RSV-B deviated strongly from neutral expectations and positive selection was detected at 20 sites in the G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and M2-2 regulatory protein. Phylogeographic reconstruction revealed a sharp decline in international viral spread during the pandemic, followed by increasing persistence. Europe consistently served as the predominant global source, followed by Western Pacific and North America. Air-travel volume was the strongest predictor of dissemination (log coefficient >0.68 for both subtypes). Post-pandemic RSV resurgence represented fundamental epidemiological restructuring shaped by a population bottleneck, positive selection and major impact of air-travel. These findings underscore the need for robust genomic surveillance to track the global circulation of lineages, and to monitor effectiveness of pharmaceutical interventions given the emergence of new genotypes.
